_comment: The map base: a hole in hell's ground, one ring deck round the void the tower stands in, with the lava river cut into it. Authored in WORLD coordinates -- instance at identity: deck at y=23.0 (r 46.7..57.3) under a rock ceiling at y=31.5 (the gallery is a cutout, open toward the void), lava sea at y=-11.05, rim at y=330. Between bearings 292.3 and 338.3 the deck is CUT AWAY and replaced, in the same mesh, by a sunken trench brimming with lava at y=22.3: the river comes out of a slot along the wall foot (head y=22.80, under the deck plane, so map_base's own shaft wall above it is never cut), runs over seven pillars (tops y=23.5) and leaves over the inner lip as one continuous sheet to y=-11.5. The shores ramp back up to deck level over 292.3-294.3 and 336.3-338.3 and share the cut edge's vertices; the pit wall's rim comes down to the river's lip, so there is no floor under the lava. Prison cells (arched glowing recesses with carved columns) are carved into the pit faces, visual only. THREE surfaces: the hell-rock atlas (rock + emissive), LavaSea -- the pit floor, on its own seamless emissive sheet -- and LavaRiver, the river and its fall, on a tiling sheet streaked along the flow and double-sided. MapBaseCollision is the purpose-built collider shipped as a `-colonly` node (deck minus the river, pit wall dropping to the trench lip over it, courtyard disc, outer wall, flat ceiling, plus the shores, pillar tops and fins); Godot turns it into a StaticBody3D + ConcavePolygonShape3D and drops its mesh, so `surfaces` counts only what is drawn.
